title: open-credits submission
description: submission.json, the data of one submission bundle: one run of the client on one copy of a work. Layers 0 to 3 of doc/data-model.md. Data only: no file path, no SQL, no contributor identity (the master takes it from the authenticated account). Every object is closed (additionalProperties false), so an unknown field, a file path among them, is rejected. References between objects (frame_ids, line_ids, entity refs) are checked by the importer, since JSON Schema cannot.

format_version.description: Version of this format (semantic versioning). The importer refuses a major version it does not know.

entities.description: Entities the client proposes for its credits: persons, companies, places, songs. Local to the bundle; the master matches them to its own entities by external ids, or sends them to the disambiguation queue.

uuid.description: UUID version 7, lower case, generated by the client. Rows that belong to the submission keep it in the master.

language.description: BCP 47 language tag: fr, en, de-CH, pt-BR.

created_at.description: When the client finished the run (UTC). The master records its own submitted_at on arrival.

ocr.description: Reproducibility: the same copy read by a better engine is a new submission.

licence.description: Every submission is placed under CC0 (charter, decision 9).

vocabulary_version.description: Version of the role vocabulary (ROLE, ROLE_MODIFIER, ROLE_ALIAS) the client parsed with, so the master knows which role codes it could have used.

has_evidence_frames.description: True when the bundle carries frames/*.webp (charter, decision 3: allowed, not mandatory).

work.description: What the credits belong to. A series or a season is never credited as such: credits are read per episode.

title_hint.description: The title as the client found it (usually from Plex), in whatever language the contributor's library uses. A sanity check on the external ids, never the work's title: the master takes original_title from TMDb or Wikidata.

title_language.description: Language of title_hint, when the client knows it (the Plex library language).

copy.description: The encode the client read. It carries no id: the master identifies it by its fingerprint, so two contributors with the same files share one copy. Grouping into an edition is done by the master and the community, from edition_hint, duration and the credits themselves.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256, in lower-case hex, of the lines '<opensubtitles_hash>:<file_size>' of the parts in part_index order, joined by '\n'.

edition_hint.description: What the contributor's library says: the Plex {edition-...} tag, FILE_EDITION (Criterion, Remastered...). Free text, never a path.

version_language.description: Language of the version the credits come from: a French dubbed copy carries French dubbing credits.

part.description: One file of the copy, identified by its content. Its path and name are never sent: they are private.

opensubtitles_hash.description: 64-bit OpenSubtitles hash (size plus first and last 64 KB), 16 lower-case hex digits. Plex computes it already.

offset_ms.description: Where the part starts in the copy: the sum of the previous parts' durations.

segment.description: Layer 1: a stretch of one part that carries credits, with its frames (layer 1), text lines (layer 2b) and blocks of credits (layer 3).

scroll_px_per_s.description: For rolling credits: measured scroll speed, which puts every frame on one virtual page.

frame.description: Layer 1: one image read by the OCR, with its text boxes (layer 2a). Frames without text are not kept.

phash.description: 64-bit perceptual hash, 16 lower-case hex digits: drops duplicates, matches frames between copies.

page_offset_px.description: For rolling credits: where the frame sits on the virtual page.

evidence.description: Optional cropped image of the frame, inside the bundle.

file.description: Path inside the zip, always frames/<frame id>.webp.

crop.description: The area of the frame the image covers, in pixels of the frame. Absent: the whole frame.

text_box.description: Layer 2a: one line box as the engine read it on one frame. Coordinates in pixels of the frame.

text_line.description: Layer 2b: one line rebuilt across frames on the virtual page, with the text chosen by vote. The pivot of the model: layer 3 can be recomputed from these lines without the video.

readings.description: How many frames saw the line.

agreeing.description: How many of them read the chosen text.

frame_ids.description: The frames that saw it: the evidence chain.

first_ms.description: First time on screen, within the part: the time index of the Wikidata reference.

block.description: Layer 3a: a heading and the credits under it, which take their context from it.

heading_raw.description: As on screen; absent for the first cast list.

unit.description: main, second_unit, additional_photography, aerial, or a place as written ("Morocco Unit").

vendor_entity_ref.description: The company whose staff the block lists.

credit.description: Layer 3b: one assertion, an entity in a role, always with the on-screen wording beside the client's interpretation.

name_raw.description: The name exactly as credited (Wikidata P1932).

entity_ref.description: The entity the client proposes, from entities[]. Absent: unresolved.

role_raw.description: The job exactly as credited (Wikidata P13187). Absent for a plain cast or thanks line with no wording.

role_code.description: The base job in the open-credits vocabulary (ROLE.code), as the client parsed it.

role_modifiers.description: ROLE_MODIFIER codes, in on-screen order: key, second, assistant, additional...

role_target_entity_ref.description: The person an assistant works for, or a stunt performer doubles.

song_ref.description: When the credit belongs to a song (performer, writer, label) rather than to the work: the song, from entities[].

is_private_individual.description: Backers, thanked persons: stored, kept out of the public view and of contributions (charter, decision 10).

entity.description: Layer 3c: an entity proposed by the client, local to the bundle.
